main_text.p: Perfectio orationis ♦Talis est perfectio mentis: sequitur perfectio orationis; quam philosophia suis præceptis ita excolit, ut eam primo puram reddat, deinde puritatem sermonis modificatione eleganti, figuratione, vocis modulatione, & gestuum insigni decore exornet. Præterea quælibet philosophiæ pars ad linguæ perfectionem facit, quando peculiares terminos præscri-bit.
Sic de fine philosophiæ latè consideratæ; sequitur de fine philosophiæ strictè consideratæ, quatenus distinguitur contra Theolo-giam, Jurisprudentiam & Medicinam.
Hic finis est partim absolutus, partim rela-tus.
Voluptas quo sensu fit finis philosophiæ.Primarius est voluptas, id est, summa animi lætitia, ex philosophicis disciplinis hausta.

Voluptatis definitio ex Aristotele.Voluptas, definitore Aristotele. 7.Eth.c.10. est actus naturæ congruus ex operatione facili, & nonim pedita. Is enim voluptate perfunditur, qui facile aliquid efficit. Voluptas ita definita, oritur vel Voluptas oritur vel ex sensu, vel ex appetitu, coq;[?]ex sensu, vel ex appetitu, vel ex intellectu. Voluptas ex sensu, puta a tactu, olfactu, in homine est no-bilior, quam in bestiis: ob id nempe, quia ipsimet sensus in homine sunt nobiliores quam in bestiis. Voluptas ex appetitu, est vel ex animali seu sensitivo, vel ex rationali seu voluntario appetitu. page.notes: Ligatures and abbreviations (æ, œ, ꝑ-type forms, tilde-free) are copied as printed. The chapter reference "Cap. XVIII." belongs to the running head, not to a heading. The marginal note's ♦ mark is a printed symbol and is kept. The left margin note "Senfitivo & Rationali" is placed at the line where it stands. The note "Voluptas oritur vel ex sensu, vel ex appetitu, coq;" ends in an unclear abbreviation. The word "nonim" and the form "ha" are read as printed but are doubtful. A small stray mark "/" stands beside "vel ex ap-" and is not transcribed.
